title: Lump in Breast

rationale.Physical Exam: Breasts / Axillae: Firm, non-tender, immobile lump. Skin dimpling. Axillary LAN.
rationale.Refer breast surgery / oncology: Lumpectomy + XRT or mastectomy + SLNB. Adjuvant therapy.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with a firm, non-tender, immobile breast lump with irregular borders, possible skin dimpling (peau d'orange), nipple retraction, or axillary lymphadenopathy. Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women. Most are invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Workup: diagnostic mammogram + breast ultrasound. If suspicious (BIRADS 4-5) → core needle biopsy for tissue diagnosis. Hormone receptor status: ER, PR, HER2/neu — guides treatment. Genetic testing: BRCA1/2 if family history, triple-negative, bilateral, or young age. Staging: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, bone scan, PET/CT if advanced. Treatment: surgery (lumpectomy + radiation vs mastectomy) + sentinel lymph node biopsy. Adjuvant therapy per receptor status: endocrine therapy (tamoxifen/AI) if ER+, HER2-directed therapy (trastuzumab) if HER2+, chemotherapy per Oncotype DX or stage.
